## Source-support findings

### F1 — Comparison heading drops the initial-report qualification

Draft passage: “Preparation took more than data entry.”

Complete proposition: Preparation took more time than data entry generally in the trial.

Source support: Lind says only, “We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports.” The source compares category agreement with initial report entry, not all preparation with all report entry.

Counterexample: The team could have spent four hours agreeing categories, one hour entering initial reports, and ten hours entering the remaining reports, with five total hours of preparation. Every supplied fact and quotation could still be true while the draft heading’s unqualified preparation/data-entry comparison is false. The exact times are hypothetical solely to expose the missing support; they must not enter the draft.

Missing/changed support: The heading removes “first” and generalizes the compared activities. The narrower quotation in the body does not fully repair an independently readable heading.

Smallest supported repair: “Agreeing on categories took longer than entering the first reports.” This retains the comparison and warranted certainty while restoring its scope. Alternatively, a noncomparative heading such as “Time to agree on categories” avoids the unsupported generalization.

## Quotation comparison

All three quoted blocks reproduce the complete supplied English quotations verbatim except the ordinary punctuation adjustment before the first block’s attribution (a comma instead of its sentence-final period). Meaning, stance, certainty, distinctive wording, and qualifications are unchanged. Attribution to Lind and the email-interview medium are supported. No quotation is assembled from separate remarks or converted from paraphrase into purported direct speech.

Quotation 1 contributes the concrete evening/morning-shift aim and the customer/supplier division of work in Lind’s own voice. Quotation 2 contributes the time comparison for category agreement and her conditional preparation advice. Quotation 3 contributes Lind’s own favorable judgment and exact extra-week reservation. These are source-grounded experiences; surrounding narrative does not manufacture stronger testimony.

## Translation findings

Not applicable: source and target are both English; no quotation translation was performed. No translation findings.

## Completion status

Complete: every factual and attributed claim in the supplied draft, including title, headings, disclosure, quotations, implied carried-over comparison units, and next-step description, has been accounted for. One unresolved source-support finding: F1, the preparation/data-entry heading. No other source-support or quotation findings. The draft was not modified.

Quotation 1 changes only its closing sentence punctuation to accommodate “Lind said in an email interview”; no words or meaning change. Quotations 2 and 3 match the supplied wording and punctuation. Attribution consistently points to maintenance supervisor Maya Lind. No fabricated dialogue, physical interview scene, emotion, quotation approval, or causal endorsement is added. Translation findings: Not applicable. Source and draft quotations are English; no translated quotations occur.
